newsitem.title: USA: U.S. proposes to cut swordfish fishing quotas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. proposes to cut swordfish fishing quotas.

text.p: The National Marine Fisheries Service on Wednesday proposed to reduce the North Atlantic swordfish fishing quota over the next three years and set a separate quota for South Atlantic swordfish.
The U.S. agency proposed to trim the North Atlantic swordfish quota from 2,625 metric tons dressed weight (mtdw) in 1996 to 2,458 in 1997, then 2,393 mtdw in 1998 and 2,327 mtdw in 1999.
The new quota for the South Atlantic stock was proposed at 187.5 mtdw for 1997.

Although the proposed North Atlantic quotas are less than in 1996, the agency said fishermen would actually be able to catch more fish because they no longer would have to count dead discards as part of the quota, unlike the last two years.
The net gain in the next three years would be 1.93 percent over the 1996 adjusted quota, it said.
The annual quota is split between two fishing seasons, from June through November and December through May.

"The reductions are intended to improve conservation and management of Atlantic swordfish," the agency said. The cuts reflected lower quotas for all Atlantic swordfish set by an international commission.
